Its large developer ecosystem could give it an advantage over Meta and Google's offerings as it potentially provides countless third-party integrations on launch. articles.headline: Making a programming language

The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. No single stage is hard - the work is in making errors useful and keeping two backends in agreement.

articles.headline: AI, work from home, and the young-graduate job market
articles.blurb: New college graduates are employed less than a few years ago. While AI may be a factor, there's growing evidence that work from home is an important factor moving the needle on young-graduate employment. AI exposure and teleworkability are highly correlated with each other, making it hard to distinguish definitively between the two factors. The full extent of AI's effects on the labor market might not manifest until the next recession.

articles.headline: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development

This ability to solve well-scoped problems is going to be an even bigger deal for machine learning research than for mathematics. AI labs mainly care about how any new algorithmic recipe empirically makes training more efficient or elicits smarter models - they don't care about theory for its own sake.

Compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen reportedly completes tasks 2.5 times faster at its default high setting, more than triples its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, and reduces fabricated claims by over fivefold. It also supports a native one-million-token input and output context, with improvements in tool recovery, multimodal reasoning, and complex agentic workflows.

articles.headline: Design is a Search Problem
articles.blurb: Design is a search problem: finding the right solution in a vast space of possibilities, which computer science's search algorithms help explain. Beam search mirrors the "show me some options" approach that AI has made far wider, while A* matches a more deliberate process steered by a good heuristic. AI has widened the beam without improving the heuristic, so empathy and taste remain the human edge.

articles.headline: Every click has a price now. Who designs how that “feels”?
articles.blurb: As AI products shift toward credit- and usage-based pricing, everyday interactions increasingly carry a visible financial cost, creating new challenges for user experience design. Unpredictable charges, unclear token consumption, and sudden usage limits can undermine trust, making transparent cost estimates, spending controls, and understandable feedback essential interface features. Designers must also decide when expensive AI processing is justified and when simpler alternatives can deliver the same result without introducing unnecessary cost or anxiety.

articles.headline: Build Faster Without Leaving Accessibility Behind

It pairs access strategies and assistive technologies with usability heuristics and standards references, in Markdown for people and YAML for agents and pipelines. ACT doesn't replace testing with disabled people or establish compliance, and its findings still need human review.

Forty-three classic logos spanning Sony, NTT, Japan Airlines, Mazda, and the Tokyo 1964 Olympics demonstrate how modernist geometry, cultural symbolism, and distinctive visual ideas helped establish recognizable identities. Many also emerged from strategic corporate identity programs, particularly those developed by PAOS, that connected visual design with broader organizational transformation.

articles.headline: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
articles.blurb: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989. Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year.
